card.name: Claim or contested-argument wording in web text
card.fires_on: Scattered words in opinion or contested-claim passages, such as 'claimed', 'claims:', 'equals', 'will' after a stated belief. Also appears partway through some words like laxatives or ALCOHOL.

modes.label: Claim verbs
modes.description: A verb or colon introducing what someone asserts or argues, often in a controversial topic.
modes.example: The only solution, it<< claimed>>, would be to increase exploitation of unconventional

modes.label: Words in the middle of contested topics
modes.description: A noun or linking word inside a polemic about pesticides, race or beliefs.
modes.example: the lamentable legacy of the benighted Rachel Carson<< and>> her acolytes.

modes.label: Inside split-up words
modes.description: A piece in the middle of a longer word such as laxatives or alcohol.

card.writes: Weakly promotes words about opacity and transparency; no clear wider effect.
card.plain: It lights up on words that introduce or carry an argued or disputed claim in opinion writing.
